name: el.runs
summary: Runs in scope: name, id, source_id, tables, signals, first_us, last_us, tags.
example:
runs = el.runs()
result = {"runs": [r["name"] for r in runs]}

name: el.signals
summary: Signal cards matching query (name, dtype, shape, table, column, per-run rows and time range).
example:
cards = el.signals("accel")
result = {"signals": [c["name"] for c in cards]}

name: el.tables
summary: Joined export tables matching query, with their columns and per-run rows.

name: el.signal
summary: One signal as a Table with columns time_us (int64, recorder clock microseconds) and value. run may be omitted when one run is in scope.

name: el.table
summary: A joined table as a Table with time_us and one column per member; a member is null on rows where it has no sample.

name: Table.select
summary: Keep only these member columns (time_us is always kept).

name: Table.count
summary: Row count without materializing the data.

name: Table.to_arrow
summary: Materialize as a pyarrow.Table; vectors are FixedSizeList. Raises ResultBudgetError beyond max_rows (default 5,000,000).

name: Table.to_polars
summary: Materialize as a polars.DataFrame; vectors are Array columns, or one column per element with flatten=True (value_x, value_y, ...).

name: el.artifacts.save_table
summary: Save a polars/pyarrow table as <name>.parquet; returns {name, path, bytes, sha256}.

name: el.artifacts.save_figure
example:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
df = el.signal("imu.temp").to_polars()
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(df["time_us"], df["value"])
result = {"figure": el.artifacts.save_figure(fig, "temp")["name"]}

name: el.artifacts.save_json
summary: Save JSON or HTML as <name>.json or <name>.html.

name: ctx.parameters
summary: The execution's parameters dict (from --param/--params or the execute tool's parameters).

name: ctx.preview
summary: At most n (cap 100) rows of a table as a list of dicts, small enough for result.
